items.title: Using uv on HPC Clusters
items.reason: Its second request seeks the same package-scoped compiled-wheel cache opt-out for environment-sensitive builds; a maintainer explicitly proposed `--no-cache-package <name>` there.

items.title: Make metadata caching of local projects opt-in when it is dynamic?
items.reason: This adjacent discussion establishes `reinstall-package` as the current mechanism for unconditional rebuild and reinstall of dynamic local packages, but it does not request strict cache bypass for arbitrary dependencies.

items.title: Allow environment variables to be included in cache keys
items.reason: This supports invalidating local-project builds when declared environment variables change, but it neither selects arbitrary dependencies nor disables cache reads and writes.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests for the proposed flag, package-specific no-cache behavior, `sync`/`run`, forced re-downloads and rebuilds, compiled-wheel caching, dynamic metadata, environment-sensitive builds, `refresh-package`, `reinstall-package`, and cache keys. Inspected candidate comments and reference chains. No pull request implementing package-scoped no-cache semantics was found. astral-sh/uv#10575 was ruled out because it concerns cache reuse across differing build configuration, while astral-sh/uv#15700 concerns mutations propagated through hard-linked files.

type_reason: The open astral-sh/uv#7642 tracks the same underlying capability: selectively disabling compiled-wheel caching for a named package whose build depends on external environment state. Its maintainer discussion explicitly identifies the proposed flag, so discussion can be centralized there.
summary: astral-sh/uv#7642 is the canonical prior request. astral-sh/uv#7282 and astral-sh/uv#10170 document narrower existing rebuild and invalidation mechanisms but do not provide strict per-package cache bypass.
draft_response:
This package-scoped cache opt-out is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#7642. The second request there covers compiled packages whose build output depends on external environment state, and the discussion specifically identifies `--no-cache-package <name>` as a possible interface. Let’s centralize the feature discussion there.

For now, the closest supported workaround is `[tool.uv] reinstall-package = ["theseus-ai"]`. That forces the named package to be reinstalled and implies a package refresh, but it does not provide the strict no-read/no-write cache behavior requested here.
